summary: Feed s120_double is degraded: IDS sees one-way traffic on 21.8% of TCP sessions (27/124) and microburst overload to 1.35 Gbps on a 1 Gbps port (135% capacity, 4 intervals). Both break stateful IDS detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is forwarding only one direction for 21.8% of TCP sessions (threshold 10%). Most likely SPAN/mirror configured TX-only or RX-only, or single-sided TAP on asymmetric path, or broker forwarding policy/filter that sends only client->server and not server->client to this tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP state tracking, handshake validation and stream reassembly. One-way flows cannot be reassembled, signatures requiring server response fail, and stateful detection is blind to server-side attacks leading to false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port so the IDS sees complete bidirectional sessions for stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts peak at 1.35 Gbps in 1 ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (135% overload, 4 intervals). Packet broker is forwarding aggregate traffic at line-rate to a single 1G tool port without load-balancing, filtering or shaping.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress drops packets during bursts. For an IDS needing full payload, any loss means missed signatures, truncated flows and attacker evasion during high-throughput periods; overload also risks tool CPU exhaustion.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute flows across 2x1G (or 1x10G) IDS ports with flow-aware hashing to absorb 1.35 Gbps bursts without loss while keeping both directions of each flow together.
